excess_kurtosis.description: Heavy Tails (Leptokurtosis): Unconditional returns exhibit heavy tails with excess kurtosis > 0 (kurtosis > 3), exceeding the Gaussian normal distribution.

hill_tail_index.description: Hill Tail Index: Power-law tail exponent alpha falls within [2.0, 5.0], characterizing the heavy-tailed, finite-variance regime universally observed in empirical finance.

return_autocorrelation.description: Absence of Linear Autocorrelations: Linear autocorrelation of returns decays rapidly to near zero (|ACF| < 0.10 for lags 1-5), consistent with the Efficient Market Hypothesis.

volatility_clustering.criterion: ACF(r^2, lag=1) > 0 and mean(ACF(r^2, lags=1..5)) > 0 with slow decay (lag_10 <= lag_1)
volatility_clustering.description: Volatility Clustering: While returns are linearly uncorrelated, squared returns exhibit positive, slowly decaying autocorrelation across lags 1-10 (ARCH effect).

spread_volatility_correlation.description: Spread-Volatility Correlation: Market makers widen bid-ask spreads during periods of elevated volatility to manage inventory risk and adverse selection.
